claims.text: Cast CoCrFeNiMn has a coarse-grained microstructure with grain sizes greater than 100 µm.
Cast CoCrFeNiMn exhibits limited ductility.
The initial CoCrFeNiMn alloy is a single-phase FCC solid solution.
Severe plastic deformation followed by sub-solvus annealing will produce a stable FCC+BCC nanocrystalline microstructure below 50 nm.
The proposed processing route will suppress intermetallic precipitation.
The processed alloy will exceed 1.2 GPa yield strength while retaining measurable ductility.
Dislocation-cell substructures created by severe plastic deformation act as nucleation sites for BCC phase formation.
A high grain-boundary density and solute drag from Cr, Mn, or Al inhibit grain growth.
Grain-boundary density and solute drag suppress diffusion-controlled sigma- and Laves-phase formation.
Local lattice distortion and stored deformation energy drive an FCC-to-BCC transformation.
Solute segregation at grain boundaries stabilizes grain sizes below 50 nm.
Hall–Petch strengthening and FCC/BCC phase-boundary strengthening increase strength by impeding dislocation motion.
Avoiding long-range ordered intermetallic phases prevents catastrophic brittle fracture.
The final equiaxed grain size will average 20–45 nm.
The final microstructure will contain 5–15 vol% uniformly dispersed BCC phase in an FCC matrix.
As-cast CoCrFeNiMn typically has a yield strength of approximately 200–300 MPa.
Annealing above 700°C causes rapid grain growth to sizes greater than 100 nm.
Annealing above 700°C nucleates brittle sigma or Laves phases because thermodynamic driving forces overcome kinetic suppression.
Al contents above 1.5 at.% without sufficient Mn cause transformation to an entirely brittle BCC structure rather than an FCC+BCC structure.
A strength increase greater than 20% relative to the SPD-only sample would demonstrate strengthening beyond simple grain refinement.

contradictions.description: The route permits high-pressure torsion, but the conditions state atmospheric pressure without limiting that condition to annealing. Atmospheric pressure is incompatible with the high-pressure stage of HPT as written.
